parts:
I installed pystan, and I think it installed okay, but then when I go to run the schools example, I run into problems. I've gotten this example (and some other simple code) to work in rstan, but I'm hoping to start using either pystan or cmdstan, since I'll be programming experiments and doing general data wrangling in python in the near future. I'm relatively new to Python, so I'm not terribly good at figuring out what's gone wrong when something has gone wrong.

Anyway, I copied the schools model and data code from https://pystan.readthedocs.org/en/latest/getting_started.html, but when I call pystan.stan, it tells me:

No handlers could be found for logger "pystan"

Then it waits a bit (while it's trying to compile the model, I believe), and then I get the following error (copied in full). I'm using a Mac with Mavericks and the Anaconda installation of Python. Any help anyone can provide would be greatly appreciated. Thanks.

Hi Noah,

(We're working on the logging error.)

It looks like Python cannot find the C++ compiler ``clang``: "/usr/bin/clang"
I thought we had figured out how to get everything working under OS X Mavericks
but apparently not. Perhaps someone else can help here.

My only pieces of advice: make sure that every piece of the core python
infrastructure (here Anacaonda) has been compiled with explicit support *for OS
X Mavericks*.

Best,

-a

messages.author: 1cd3ce37d8489fec
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Problems with pystan eight schools example (and maybe installation?)
parts:
Hi Allen and Noah,

I have a question related to the logging error that you both mentioned, which I also encounter every time I run models.  What exactly does this error mean and what effect does it have?

The reason I ask is that I have found that Pystan does not pass along information about parsing errors that prevent stan code from compiling.  For example, if you fail to leave a semicolon at the end of a line, Rstan will tell you:

DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:
Parser expecting: ";"

Whereas Pystan will not return this information, and only raises a ValueError.  I was planning to open an issue for this on GitHub, but perhaps this is the logging error being referred to and the development team is already well aware of the behavior.

Best,

~Nathan

My only pieces of advice: make sure that every piece of the core python
infrastructure (here Anacaonda) has been compiled with explicit support *for OS
X Mavericks*.

Best,

-a
